params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The television holds dark and dead still for one beat. Then its screen flares pale in one hard flash and a jagged line draws itself across it in one fast stroke, starting low in the lower left corner, dipping once, and then shooting up and to the right, steeper and steeper, until its arrowhead rockets clean off the top edge of the screen, and the whole picture jolts happily with it — the shelf brackets shiver, the taped sketches on the wall flutter, and the hanging cable swings and settles. The screen stays lit and holds with the line on it, and the sketches settle back against the wall.

From the moment it lights, the screen stays pale and shows the same climbing line in every frame after the line has been drawn, with no words on it. The television, its shelf and brackets, the shelf of binders at the left and the taped sketches at the right stay the same drawings in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
